title: What survives an exec
summary: An ignored signal stays ignored after exec; a handler does not.
hints: Ignoring is inherited by `fork` AND kept by `exec`. A handler function is inherited by `fork`, but `exec` replaces the program, so the disposition goes back to the default.
`signal(SIGINT, SIG_IGN)` ignores, `signal(SIGINT, SIG_DFL)` restores the default, `signal(SIGINT, f)` installs a handler `void f(int)` (an empty one is enough).
`WIFSIGNALED(status)` is true when the child was killed by a signal and `WTERMSIG(status)` tells which; otherwise use `WEXITSTATUS`.
